dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There are a few more letters here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Take your pick, {NICKNAME}. Let's read one.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (VII)
response.text: To D:

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (VII)
response.text: Per standard procedure, the Knights of Favonius needs to take a statement from all relevant parties.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (VII)
response.text: Recently, the Knights of Favonius have received reports from a number of eye-witnesses claiming to have seen the Darknight Hero in the vicinity of the Dawn Winery.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (VII)
response.text: The Grand Master has assigned the Cavalry Company to this mission. As such, I will be paying you a visit in three days.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (VII)
response.text: He seems to think that our relationship can be improved if we are forced to talk in person.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (VII)
response.text: Don't worry, though. My lips are sealed. This will be nothing more than a formality. Anyway, three days' notice should be enough for you, I presume?

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (VIII)
response.text: To D:

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (VIII)
response.text: The appearance of the Darknight Hero has indeed bought the Knights of Favonius some valuable time during the Abyss Order's last attack.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (VIII)
response.text: This helped Jean convince the Knights of Favonius to stop focusing on trying to stop him.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (VIII)
response.text: This will decrease the limits on the Darknight Hero's actions, but this doesn't mean that his situation will necessarily improve.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (VIII)
response.text: Objects with too honed an edge tend to be damaged more easily. You, I'm sure, are aware of the great dangers that come with acting alone.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (VIII)
response.text: That said, I would advise against such a course of action.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (IX)
response.text: To D:

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (IX)
response.text: I heard that the Dawn Winery did not suffer any damage. Likewise, the Knights of Favonius only sustained minor injuries, and will recover quickly.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (IX)
response.text: However, an employee of a local merchant has gone missing, and their last known location just so happens to align with the Abyss Order's area of activity.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (IX)
response.text: The Knights have dispatched people to go to the rescue.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (IX)
response.text: Do be aware that the Abyss Order has become more dangerous as of late, even going so far as to organize multi-pronged offensives.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (IX)
response.text: Perhaps the Darknight Hero and the Knights of Favonius should team up. That might guarantee that things will go off without a hitch, hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, there's another bunch of letters here... Diluc must have read these ones recently, too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Which one shall we read first?

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (I)
response.text: To D:

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (I)
response.text: A storm is brewing within the Knights of Favonius. Varka's inner circle is preparing to investigate Eroch and his henchmen, and it's looking increasingly likely that Eroch is about to get unseated from that high horse of his.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (I)
response.text: You might not be too pleased to see this letter of mine, but I mean to get this news to you as soon as possible.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (I)
response.text: You don't have to reply.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (II)
response.text: To D:

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (II)
response.text: Even I was a little surprised to hear that you'd decided to leave on a trip.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (II)
response.text: Jean wanted to write and try to dissuade you, but I advised her against it.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (II)
response.text: As for Varka, I don't think he knows about this. Otherwise, he'd have probably sat you down for a talk.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (II)
response.text: If you'd like to leave, do it now. The less the people know, the less the goodbyes you'll have to say. Leave at night, too, so things won't be too saddening.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (II)
response.text: Take care.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (III)
response.text: To D:

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (III)
response.text: Some slightly bad news. Eroch won't be quite so difficult to bring down after all.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (III)
response.text: The Grand Master's order to investigate has certainly dealt him a major blow, but I wouldn't call the problem "pulled up by the roots" yet.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (III)
response.text: The matter's been handed over to Jean's jurisdiction. She'll take care of this, I believe. Eroch is an obstacle in her path, in any case.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (III)
response.text: Just sit tight and wait for the good news.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: There, it's done.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: The ley line deposit will disappear before long.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: All thanks to the power of teamwork!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: See, even Captain Pyro needs his trusty sidekicks sometimes. It can't be Master Diluc saving the day by himself every single time. Many hands make light work!

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Sidekicks, hmm...

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: It's been a long time since I last worked with others. It's not so bad.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: If the opportunity arises, let's team up again in the future.

choices.text: That battle was a lot of fun.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Another bunch of letters?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Which one do you think we should start with, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (IV)
response.text: To D:

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (IV)
response.text: Recently, a group of businessmen returned to Mondstadt. Word is that the reason for their return is a downturn in business.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (IV)
response.text: According to my observations, their employees are regulars at Angel's Share. These people can also be found out in the more dangerous parts of the wilds around the city.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (IV)
response.text: Now, a few of them were a little careless and even dropped some pages of their notes on the ground. I took the liberty of returning these sheets to the Angel's Share. You know, out of the goodness of my heart.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (IV)
response.text: I think they might have something to do with you, seeing as how they were there. I also noticed that their notes were written in code. Information brokers, perhaps? Or some kind of secret organization?

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (IV)
response.text: Whatever the case, it took quite a lot of effort to see those blurred words with only one eye, you know? Don't worry, I'll keep this a secret.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (V)
response.text: To D:

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (V)
response.text: I didn't try to hide it from you on purpose, you know. But I suppose you found out all the same, huh?

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (V)
response.text: I mean, not everyone who wears an eyepatch must be blind, right? Don't people also wear an eyepatch if they have a scar over their right eye?

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (V)
response.text: The long-awaited good news is finally here.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (V)
response.text: Now, I'm going to bring a glass of wine when I go to watch Eroch pack his things and leave on his last day (good riddance, by the way). That should be fun, eh?

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (V)
response.text: I know you're not the type to do that sort of thing, but I am, so allow me.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (VI)
response.text: To D:

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (VI)
response.text: Oh, my! No sooner did you get back than a mysterious character started popping up.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (VI)
response.text: I hear he's called the Darknight Hero. He has repeatedly fought off Treasure Hoarders and monsters in the Mondstadt area — and he's even attacked Abyss Order strongholds.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (VI)
response.text: So far, it seems like he is on Mondstadt's side, but the Knights of Favonius could never permit the existence of a vigilante.

response.speaker: A Letter in Beautiful Handwriting (VI)
response.text: I get the feeling that the two of you would get along nicely. Why don't you find an opportunity to get to know him and give him some sage advice? You know, just so he doesn't get caught by the Knights?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There are two notes here. Which one shall we start with?

response.speaker: The First Note
response.text: It's been years since the ley lines last released such highly aggressive monsters during an anomaly.

response.speaker: The First Note
response.text: The Darknight Hero's timing was perfect. The way he lured the monsters a few at a time into the open to defeat them one by one... quite the strategy.

response.speaker: The First Note
response.text: And then he pretended to be seriously injured, luring out the Abyss Order's main forces and then meeting them head on. A truly magnificent counterattack.

response.speaker: The First Note
response.text: Still, this plan involved too many uncertainties. The Darknight Hero himself even said that he can't afford to take risks like this every time.

response.speaker: The First Note
response.text: Getting to the root of the problem and preventing these types of ley line disorders from happening is the safest approach.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon didn't follow all of that. Eh, but it seemed to be about a previous battle Diluc was in?

response.speaker: The Second Note
response.text: Ley lines hold many secrets. We ordinary people do not need to concern ourselves with the way they work.

response.speaker: The Second Note
response.text: But since the Darknight Hero will be fighting against the Abyss Order for the long term, it is in our best interests to gain a deeper understanding of them.

response.speaker: The Second Note
response.text: I heard that the captain of the Knights of Favonius Investigation Team is a highly accomplished academic, but unlike Lisa, he is not especially close with the Acting Grand Master.

response.speaker: The Second Note
response.text: We should be able to learn a few things from him without the Knights of Favonius finding out.

response.speaker: The Second Note
response.text: Perhaps the Darknight Hero could ask him for input on the technical issues regarding the ley lines. I will deliver the letter to his camp on the mountain.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Sounds like it was talking about Albedo. Did Diluc write a letter to Albedo?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A Letter With Elegant Handwriting

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: Dear Diluc,

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: Welcome back to Mondstadt, Sir.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: It has been some time since the incident. We discovered that Eroch had betrayed us, and he has been punished severely.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: I hope that this news will put your mind at ease.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: In other news, our people have discovered that the Abyss Order has stepped up its activities between Wolvendom and Stone Gate lately.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: Also — a mysterious individual that people are calling the "Darknight Hero" has suddenly started showing up out of nowhere all around Mondstadt City. He typically acts in the dead of night, and his intentions are currently unclear.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: Please stay safe, and notify the Knights as soon as possible should you see anything suspicious. We will send support immediately.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: Whether you are presently in our ranks or not, all faithful knights will remember your contributions to the Knights of Favonius.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Elegant Handwriting
dialogues.text: May you remain in good health.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A Neatly Written Letter

dialogues.speaker: A Neatly Written Letter
dialogues.text: Dear Mr. Diluc,

dialogues.speaker: A Neatly Written Letter
dialogues.text: It is my pleasure to investigate the ley lines alongside you.

dialogues.speaker: A Neatly Written Letter
dialogues.text: As you know, my focus is on alchemy, so my knowledge of the ley lines remains quite shallow, and I fear that I will only be able to share what little understanding I have.

dialogues.speaker: A Neatly Written Letter
dialogues.text: According to many pre-existing documents, the ley lines can be seen as a medium for storing information. Under certain circumstances, they can record activities that occur in the area around them.

dialogues.speaker: A Neatly Written Letter
dialogues.text: All this information goes through a recording and storage process. After a certain period of time, they may be released once again by the ley lines.

dialogues.speaker: A Neatly Written Letter
dialogues.text: If I may be so bold as to make a guess, there should be a method to activate the ley lines. Those who grasp such methods can control the times at which ley line information is recorded and released.

dialogues.speaker: A Neatly Written Letter
dialogues.text: Judging from the runic symbols and some other clues, I surmise that there are particular members of the Abyss Order who may have a very small chance of being able to achieve this.

dialogues.speaker: A Neatly Written Letter
dialogues.text: If you believe that this requires further investigation, these entities may serve as your point of entry.

dialogues.speaker: A Neatly Written Letter
dialogues.text: I wrote a paper a few years ago in which I covered my brief foray into questions concerning the flow of ley lines and other such topics. You will find a copy of this paper enclosed.

dialogues.speaker: A Neatly Written Letter
dialogues.text: I hope that it can help to clear up some of your doubts.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A Letter With Rough Handwriting

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: Diluc,

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: Jean wrote to me lately with shocking news. If I don't miss my guess, she wrote to you too. Her sentiments are those of the Knights as a whole.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: Crepus was a good man, and I thought very well of him. It grieves me greatly to know that he met with such a fate.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: As for the defeat of the drake, the honors for that accomplishment should go to your father. I do not accept Eroch's theft of the credit for that deed, which was bought with your father's sacrifice.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: Stolen credit will not be accepted within the Knights of Favonius under any circumstances. I will not permit it.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: I have already given Jean the authority to punish Eroch with all necessary severity. The Knights will inform you of the results.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: I've heard that you've been taking some time off outdoors and may not be easy to reach, so there is no guarantee that my letter will reach you. As such, I'll stop here for now.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: If it does reach you, then I wish you good health and safety in your travels. Contact us if you need anything.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: I hope that falcon of yours will help put this letter in your hands. I mean, I don't write in person very often, you know?

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: These may seem like pointless words to you right now, but remember: even the greatest of disasters must come to an end.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Rough Handwriting
dialogues.text: Mondstadt waits for your return, and if you're willing, the Knights will always welcome you. (If you're not, forget I said anything, yeah?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A Tidily Written Letter

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: To the heir of the Ragnvindr Clan,

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: I apologize for sending this letter without notice. You may not remember me, but we've met a few times.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: We've met near the square, when I sat at the table adjacent to yours at the Good Hunter, and I've seen you in your tavern...

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: You were always busy with a great many things, especially back when you were much chattier than you are now. You spoke cheerfully and often with your brother and friends then.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: It's probably no surprise that you did not notice me then. But I've always had my eye on you, child.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: I recall with crystal clarity how my little Klee once made a complete mess of your vineyard while she was trying to catch Crystalflies there...

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: But you didn't get angry. In fact, you personally escorted Klee back and even gave her a few bottles of fresh grape juice.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: Now I think that might jog your memory, yes?

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: Klee recently told me that she "hasn't seen that strange man with the red hair in aaages," so I decided to look into it out of curiosity.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: My deepest condolences regarding your father.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: In many of the stories I've been told, you are the model knight: proud, driven, a knight of noble character and lineage.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: But I know that you're gentler than you appear. If you weren't, you wouldn't have treated Klee the way you did.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: And since you helped my child out, I hope you won't mind if I treat you as if you were my own.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: Therefore, I sincerely hope that you will leave the dark place that you are presently in, and that you will not wallow in grief and remorse.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: Partings are most painful things, but they also encourage us to grow. A bird that has lost the roof over its head will fly further than others of its kind.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: Go out and see the world. That's the best course of action I can envision. Only by feeling, observing, and listening can your heart be healed.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: Parents all wish that they can accompany their children forever, and the skies, seas, and stars bear witness to that oath.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: Everything that was your father now finds new life with you. That which you will experience in this world may have been things that your father experienced once upon a time.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: I hope that the wind will bring you all manner of wondrous things in your journeys to come.

dialogues.speaker: A Tidily Written Letter
dialogues.text: In any case, keep your chin up, young child.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A Letter With Clear Handwriting

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Clear Handwriting
dialogues.text: Master,

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Clear Handwriting
dialogues.text: Master Kaeya took leave and stayed at Dawn Winery for a few days.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Clear Handwriting
dialogues.text: In a rare turn of events, he decided to stay in his original bedroom. He would pace about the grounds when idle, and even asked Adelinde to make him his favorite dishes.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Clear Handwriting
dialogues.text: Ah, it really does take me back.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Clear Handwriting
dialogues.text: I shall be honest with you, but I was quite surprised to hear Master Kaeya say that he wanted to stay for a few days.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Clear Handwriting
dialogues.text: We did not refuse him, however. We believe that even if you were here, you would not refuse him outright.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Clear Handwriting
dialogues.text: Dawn Winery has always been a more quiet location, perhaps because all who stay here are rather peaceable people.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Clear Handwriting
dialogues.text: The house is made by those who live in it, and Master Kaeya's uncommon arrival did end up livening the place up significantly.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Clear Handwriting
dialogues.text: I hope that you are doing well in your travels abroad. Everyone here at the winery misses you.

dialogues.speaker: A Letter With Clear Handwriting
dialogues.text: May you remain safe and in good health.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A New Letter

dialogues.speaker: A New Letter
dialogues.text: Dear Darknight Hero, the Knights of Favonius have stepped up the guard details throughout Mondstadt without making any major movements. The Abyss Order will not have noticed.

dialogues.speaker: A New Letter
dialogues.text: I am scouting around Dragonspine. The monsters here are scattered and separated. Clearly, they haven't been assembled by the Abyss Order.

dialogues.speaker: A New Letter
dialogues.text: There are no signs of enemy activity in the south of Mondstadt either.

dialogues.speaker: A New Letter
dialogues.text: If you can confirm that the other locations are also free of monsters, we will be able to conclude that the Abyss Order has nothing to do with the recent ley line disorder.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to the Acting Grand Master
dialogues.text: Dear Jean,

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to the Acting Grand Master
dialogues.text: Thank you for your concern, Acting Grand Master. It is as you say. That incident should no longer weigh heavily on my mind.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to the Acting Grand Master
dialogues.text: Punishing Eroch for his malfeasance was the right way to correct the Knights of Favonius's past mistakes. This is an important step indeed for the Knights.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to the Acting Grand Master
dialogues.text: As for my own personal safety, you need not concern yourself too much. The Knights of Favonius should focus their efforts where it counts by looking after those who need it most.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to the Acting Grand Master
dialogues.text: May you also remain in good health.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to Mr. Albedo
dialogues.text: Dear Albedo,

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to Mr. Albedo
dialogues.text: Thank you for the detailed explanation. I have read your paper and found it both enriching and easy to understand. It is a rare and well-written document indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to Mr. Albedo
dialogues.text: I have written the relevant information down in hopes that it will be put to good use in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to Mr. Albedo
dialogues.text: Guarding against danger is a very important skill. I will continue to keep watching over the Abyss Order, and use force against them where necessary.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to Grand Master Varka
dialogues.text: Dear Master Varka,

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to Grand Master Varka
dialogues.text: You have my utmost thanks for your condolences and concern. My father would be pleased to have heard your compliments.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to Grand Master Varka
dialogues.text: I doubt that anything would have pleased him more than to have the acknowledgment of the Knight of Boreas.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to Grand Master Varka
dialogues.text: I am presently traveling, and by a stroke of fortune, your letter has indeed reached me safely.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to Grand Master Varka
dialogues.text: If nothing goes awry, I believe that I will not be rejoining the Knights of Favonius. However, I will not forget my previous experiences. I will commit everything the Knights taught me to heart.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to Grand Master Varka
dialogues.text: May this find you in good health.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (There's something strange about this brick...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Take this brick off the wall

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It's a secret compartment... with a box inside.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Open the box

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Box in a Secret Compartment
dialogues.text: The objects in the box are all pretty old. One particular sheet of paper stands out.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Box in a Secret Compartment
dialogues.text: A piece of it has been burned away, and the remaining parts show signs of having been rescued from that same flame.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Box in a Secret Compartment
dialogues.text: Every line on this sheet of paper has a matching one right under it. From the handwriting, it looks like a child wrote on this first before an adult stepped in, held their hand, and taught them how to do it the second time.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Box in a Secret Compartment
dialogues.text: The writings are as follows: "Remember always that it was the Alberich Clan, who did not have royal blood, who stepped in as regents when the strength of the one-eyed king Irmin failed."

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Box in a Secret Compartment
dialogues.text: "Though we could not restore Khaenri'ah to life, we of the Alberich Clan should lead lives as those who blaze like fire, rather than those who wallow in the embers."

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Box in a Secret Compartment
dialogues.text: If you flip the paper over, there are other words there. You reckon these must be annotations of some sort.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Box in a Secret Compartment
dialogues.text: "I saved this one memento from the fire 'Father' made while he wasn't paying attention. This was in violation of our principles. Our clan's affairs should never be recorded."

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Box in a Secret Compartment
dialogues.text: "For me, this sheet of paper cannot serve as any form of identification, and will not give me passage anywhere."

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Box in a Secret Compartment
dialogues.text: "Now that I look at it, his handwriting was as grieving as a smoking ash pile. There is no way that I can write something like that, living in Mondstadt as I am."

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Box in a Secret Compartment
dialogues.text: Moving the paper aside, you can see a cloth bag underneath it that contains an eyepatch of significant age. A sticker is attached to the side, and the text on it reads:

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Box in a Secret Compartment
dialogues.text: "Hah! To think that all that play-acting as a one-eyed pirate would eventually end with one actual wounded eye."

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Box in a Secret Compartment
dialogues.text: "I have never blamed Diluc for that. I suppose I must have been asking for it, telling him the truth the day my adoptive father died without expecting conflict to emerge somehow."

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Box in a Secret Compartment
dialogues.text: "He seems to believe that I really was blinded, though that's not the case. Well, I've fooled him for a while, haven't I? Might as well keep going."

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Box in a Secret Compartment
dialogues.text: Two letters lie beneath the bag, all of which have "D" as their sender. The letters are in great condition, and there is a time written on the back. This is most likely the time these letters were received.

dialogues.speaker: Mysterious Box in a Secret Compartment
dialogues.text: You can tell that the words have been written in a strong but elegant hand.

response.speaker: Letter Addressed to "K" (I)
response.text: To K:

response.speaker: Letter Addressed to "K" (I)
response.text: Message received. Thank you.

response.speaker: Letter Addressed to "K" (I)
response.text: Also, I suggest that you stop mentioning eyes in your letters. Don't think that I don't know that your right eye wasn't blinded.

response.speaker: Mysterious Box in a Secret Compartment
response.text: A small paper bag lies next to these two letters. It contains nothing but a few seashells.

response.speaker: Mysterious Box in a Secret Compartment
response.text: They have lost most of their luster. It is unclear how much time has passed since they were picked up.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (It might be best to store this box and restore everything to how it was originally.)

response.speaker: Letter Addressed to "K" (II)
response.text: To K:

response.speaker: Letter Addressed to "K" (II)
response.text: Thanks for the letter.

response.speaker: Letter Addressed to "K" (II)
response.text: Cooperating with the Knights has objective pros and cons, like two sides of a coin. I'm sure you understand that better than I do.

response.speaker: Letter Addressed to "K" (II)
response.text: No need to worry about my safety. Self-preservation is easy. Striving towards my goal is hard. Take better care of yourself instead.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to Ms. Alice
dialogues.text: Dear Ms. Alice,

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to Ms. Alice
dialogues.text: I must admit that when I read the opening lines of this letter, I was not expecting it to have been written by you.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to Ms. Alice
dialogues.text: It seems that I may have indeed failed to notice you despite your presence nearby. My apologies for that.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to Ms. Alice
dialogues.text: Regarding Klee, I have heard that you are an extremely powerful witch, so I suspect that Klee would have been just fine even sans my presence.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to Ms. Alice
dialogues.text: Even so, you sent me this letter, for which I am thankful.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to Ms. Alice
dialogues.text: As you have said, traveling is my best option at present. I will go out and experience all that the world has to offer, just as you have suggested.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to Ms. Alice
dialogues.text: My father's will shall find continuation through me.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to Ms. Alice
dialogues.text: Klee is welcome to stay at Dawn Winery as a guest during my absence. Adelinde will prepare sufficient snacks and grape juice for such occasions. And if you don't mind, you are also welcome to drop by.

dialogues.speaker: Letter Addressed to Ms. Alice
dialogues.text: I hope that you and Klee stay in good health.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These letters cover a whole load of different events. Paimon never knew Diluc's past was so complicated...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're really gonna have to study all the details to figure out how everything fits together.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
